stories.title: Bank of Canada expected to keep rates unchanged in December after flat October inflation
stories.summary: Statistics Canada reported that Canada’s consumer price index was unchanged year‑over‑year in October at 3.1%, matching September’s rate, while core inflation excluding energy fell to 2.0% from 2.1% the month before. Gas prices surged, rising 30.9% compared with September. Economists said the flat CPI reading makes a December policy‑rate hold more likely.
stories.why: Inflation data can shift expectations for central-bank interest rates, bond yields, borrowing costs and household purchasing power.
stories.previousTitle: Bank of Canada likely to hold policy rate steady in December after flat October CPI
stories.previousSummary: Statistics Canada reported that the consumer price index for October rose 3.1 % year‑over‑year, unchanged from September and driven mainly by high energy prices. Economists cited the data as indicating that inflation is not spreading beyond energy costs and said it raises the likelihood that the Bank of Canada will keep its benchmark interest rate unchanged at its December 9 meeting. The central bank had raised the policy rate in October, its first hike since July 2023.

stories.title: Indian shares rise on Tuesday on foreign inflows and earnings
stories.summary: Indian equities traded higher on Tuesday, extending the rally in the Sensex and Nifty as record foreign inflows and resilient corporate earnings supported the market. Auto, PSU bank and other bank stocks led gains, while FMCG, pharma, financial services and metal stocks also advanced. Senco Gold surged over 8% after reporting its highest‑ever festive‑season retail sales of more than Rs 2,426 crore.
stories.why: The rally shows broad investor confidence in India’s market fundamentals.

stories.title: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem to Leave Office in 2027
stories.summary: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem announced he will not seek a second term, so his seven‑year tenure will end on June 2, 2027. The central bank confirmed the decision on Monday and said it has begun a search for his successor, aiming to complete the appointment by the spring of 2027. The announcement initiates a leadership transition at Canada’s monetary authority.
stories.why: A new governor will shape future monetary‑policy decisions, affecting inflation and financial‑market conditions.

stories.title: OpenAI adds CSAM image classifier and ChatGPT warnings
stories.summary: OpenAI announced a new image classifier that detects child sexual abuse material, including AI‑generated images, and is being made available through its API to selected companies at no charge. In early testing the classifier reduced the number of flagged images by 48% while still identifying the same amount of abusive content, and images it flags are twice as likely to be abusive. ChatGPT will now show warning screens for prompts that sexualize children, provide support resources, and temporarily suspend accounts for 24 hours on a first offense.
stories.why: The tools are intended to limit the distribution of illegal CSAM and reduce reviewer workload.

stories.title: US to require licenses for AI chip and server exports to any data centre that could serve restricted countries
stories.summary: The U.S. Commerce Department is preparing an interim rule that will require companies to obtain licenses before exporting, re‑exporting, or transferring AI chips and server hardware to data centres anywhere in the world if the equipment could provide compute to entities in China or other nations on the D:5 embargo list. The rule extends existing controls that already mandate licenses for direct shipments of AI chips to those countries, targeting remote‑access pathways.
stories.why: Trade developments can affect currencies, business costs, market access and the external balance of the economies involved.
stories.previousTitle: U.S. prepares interim rule tightening AI chip export controls
stories.previousSummary: The U.S. Commerce Department announced an interim rule that will require licenses for any export, reexport, or transfer of AI chips and server hardware to data centers worldwide if the equipment could be used to provide compute to entities in China or other countries on the D:5 embargo list, which includes Russia, Iran, North Korea and 18 others. The rule expands existing controls that already mandate licenses for direct shipments of AI chips to those jurisdictions, aiming to block remote access to U.S. AI infrastructure.
